name: Del Haskins
lines: *Del shakes rain off his cap. He looks pale.
Hey, kid. Gimme one of those VOLT things. I need to stay sharp tonight.
Nearly hit somebody on the curve. Little girl. Yellow raincoat. Standing right in the road.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Gray around the mouth. His hands won't stop shaking.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal.

reply: I got out to look. Nobody there. Just wet footprints going toward the water. Little ones.
Then something big stepped out of the trees behind them. Tall. Real tall. I got back in the truck.

talk.text: Maybe pull over and sleep for a while.
reply: Can't. Got a load due in Holloway at six. I'll be fine. Always am.

lines: Thanks, kid. Hey — if I don't come by tomorrow, don't worry about it, all right?
*He climbs back into his rig. His taillights disappear around the reservoir curve.
Coffee works. Thanks, kid.
*He climbs back into his rig. His taillights disappear around the reservoir curve.
Fine. I'll manage.
*His taillights disappear around the reservoir curve.

name: College Student
lines: *The student from the first night. Same hoodie. Same 3% phone.
Hi — sorry — do you have anything with caffeine? I've got four more hours of driving.
...Wait. Have I been here before?
payment: Exact change. Same coins as last time, you'd swear.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Exhausted. Confused. Real.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection is already there — it was standing at the machine before she arrived.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE 104  TEMP 36.5°C  RESIDUE: MODERATE (repeated exposure)

cameras.note: CAM 2 shows two of her: one at the machine, one standing a little behind, looking at the booth.

talk.text: You were here three nights ago.
reply: No — I left Holloway tonight. I've never... my GPS keeps routing me back here. Every time I take the curve, I end up at this stop.
That's not possible, right? Tell me that's not possible.

lines: Thanks. Okay. I'm going to take the other road this time.
*She leaves. Her extra reflection doesn't. It stays at the glass until you look away.
Thanks. I'm taking the other road this time.
Okay. Okay. I'll just... go.

name: The Passenger
lines: *Mr. Crane, dry again, glasses fogged.
Evening! Is the 2:58 running late?
I've lost my ticket, I think. Have you seen it? Brown stub, Meridian Coach Lines.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: He looks at you like he's trying to remember something you told him. Something important.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: The same polite, harried face. He doesn't remember you at all.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection is wet to the knees.

reply: *He goes still.
October. Yes. That's right. How did you know that?
...You told me something, didn't you. Before. I can't hold onto it.

talk.text: "Mr. Crane. Remember what I told you."
reply: *He closes his eyes.
Twenty-twenty-six. Yes. I remember now. It comes and goes.

lines: Thank you. You're very kind. I feel like you're always very kind.
*He goes back to the stop.
Oh. All right.

name: The Collector
lines: *The Collector, ledger tucked under one arm.
Good evening again. You'll have noticed the handbook has been updated. Rules change. That's what makes them interesting.
I'd like to make you a better offer. Anything from Row E. Twenty-five dollars.
Or — if Row E is empty — just your receipt roll. The used one.
requestText: Anything from Row E, or your used receipt roll
payment: Twenty-five dollars in bills with no faces on them.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: There is a face under the hat. You are fairly sure of that. You can't say anything else about it.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection is writing in the ledger, even though he isn't.

inspect.label: Ledger
inspect.text: The ledger is open a crack. The newest line has your handwriting on it.

cameras.note: CAM 2: no one at the unit.

talk.text: "Did you put that page in my handbook?"
reply: *He chuckles.
I don't work for Meridian. I'm their client. A client may make suggestions.
Whether you follow them is entirely your business.

talk.text: Give him the used receipt roll.

lines: That isn't what I asked for. But I'll remember the gesture.
*You hand him the curl of used receipts. Every one of your transactions. Every customer's name.
He tucks it into his ledger like a pressed flower.
Very good. Very, very good.
You're consistent. I admire consistency. It makes people so easy to predict.
*He's gone.
*He accepts the warm can, turns it in his glove, and smiles beneath the brim.
Thank you. Our account grows.

name: The Silent Child
lines: *The girl in the yellow raincoat, rain beading on her hood.
*She presses a new drawing to the glass, then taps the salt slot. She mimes pouring something in a line on the ground.
*She points toward the bus stop, where a woman's silhouette waits in the rain.
payment: She leaves the drawing on the tray.

inspect.label: Drawing
inspect.text: The machine, drawn row by row in crayon. Behind the glass, between the cans, a woman's face with a name tag that says 0.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: She's trembling. She keeps glancing at the bus stop.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection matches her.

cameras.note: CAM 1: the Smiling Woman is standing at the bus stop, facing the machine. She is not moving.

reply: *She points at the bus stop. She makes a face with a huge smile using her fingers. Then she draws a line in the air between herself and the stop.

lines: *She takes the packet and pours a careful line of salt across the edge of the lot, between the machine and the bus stop.
*Out at the stop, the woman's silhouette takes one step forward. Then stops. Then steps back.
*The girl looks at you and, for the first time, almost smiles.
*She takes the gum but keeps pointing at the salt slot, urgently. Then she runs.
*She shakes her head and points at the salt again. Then she runs.
*She leaves the drawing and runs into the rain.

name: The Drenched Man?
lines: *The Drenched Man shuffles up to the machine, soaked, dripping.
...Water. Please.
It's so dry. Down there. So dry.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Gray skin, blue lips, clouded eyes. It is Walter's face. It is exactly Walter's face, as if copied from a photograph.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Its reflection doesn't move with it. When it sways, the reflection stays still — and then turns its head to look at you on its own.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Under the brighter tubes: the reflection is not wet at all. It is grinning.

inspect.label: Coins
inspect.text: The quarters are dry. Walter's were always wet.

inspect.label: Uniform
inspect.text: MERIDIAN COACH LINES. The name tag says W. PRUITT, but the letters are backwards, like they were copied from a reflection.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  RESIDUE: ABNORMAL — MATCHES NO RECORDED PATTERN.  DISPOSITION: HUNGRY. HUNGRY. HUNGRY.

cameras.note: CAM 1: the figure at the machine. Far behind it, at the edge of the reservoir, another soaked man in a driver's uniform is standing still, watching.
CAM 4: Walter Pruitt is standing on the road shoulder, a long way from the machine, shaking his head.

reply: Yes. Yes. Walter. Walter. That's me. Water, please.
...Route. Yes. The route. Water, please.

lines: *It takes the bottle. It doesn't drink. It opens its mouth, and keeps opening it.
*The water in the bottle — in every bottle in the machine — begins to boil.
*It drops the item without looking at it.
Water.
*It leaves, and its reflection leaves a few seconds later, walking backwards.
*For a moment its face slides, like wet paper, and there's nothing underneath.
*Then it's Walter's face again, smiling far too wide, and it walks backwards into the dark.
*It waits. Its reflection waits longer. Eventually both are gone.

name: The Drenched Man
lines: *Another soaked man shuffles up. Walter — the real one. His coins drip on the counter.
Did you give that thing water?
...Good. Good. Don't ever. It learns faces. It learned mine.
Water, please. If you'll still have me.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection drips in time with him. It moves exactly as he does.

inspect.label: Coins
inspect.text: Wet. Always wet.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Sad, patient, unmistakably the same man as the first night.

cameras.note: Not on CAM 2, like the first night. The puddle spreads the same way.

reply: They pulled my bus out of the reservoir in '88. Meridian did. Didn't scrap it.
They built that machine out of it. That's why we come here, all of us. It's the last stop.
Something was standing in the road. Tall. In a long coat. I swerved.
I keep thinking if I'd just hit him...

lines: *He drinks, slow this time.
Thank you. One more and I think I'll be ready. Ready to go.
*He walks back toward the water.
*He nods.
I understand. Hard to tell us apart now.

name: The Smiling Woman
lines: *Mrs. Marsh, at the edge of the light.
Hello, dear. You've seen her again, haven't you? She leaves salt everywhere. Such a messy child.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: She stays well back, on the far side of the salt line. Her smile is very wide, and very still.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: She's close to the glass. Close enough that her breath should fog it. It doesn't.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection has its hands pressed to the glass from the inside.

talk.text: "She was here. She was scared of you."
reply: Scared? Of her own mother?
*The smile doesn't move. Something behind it does.
Thank you, dear. That's very helpful.

talk.text: "I don't know where your daughter is."
reply: You're a terrible liar. I like that in an attendant.

lines: *She takes the gum without looking at it.
She'll come for it. They always come for the sweet things.
*She lets it fall.
*She tries to step closer, and can't. The salt line glitters.
*Her smile stays. Her eyes don't.
*She slaps her palm against the glass. The whole machine rings like a bell.
Another time.
